reviewContext.executionCapability: This review was performed with Bash/network execution access (per the contract's Execution-Tooling Note) and live/testnet Base Sepolia chain access. All node --test suites were independently re-run by this adversary; Tier-3 was independently re-attacked live against the real facilitator + real ERC-8004 registry with fresh, adversary-authored transaction hashes and timestamps.

evidence.description: isLockStale(nowMs, mtimeMs, staleMs) is exported (`export function isLockStale(...)`) and is a pure boolean expression `(nowMs - mtimeMs) > staleMs`. acquire() calls tryCreateLockFile() then, on failure, reclaimStaleLock(file, staleMs), which calls `isLockStale(Date.now(), stat.mtimeMs, staleMs)` BY NAME -- no inline `Date.now() - stat.mtimeMs > staleMs` comparison exists anywhere in acquire()'s own body.

Independently re-run 3x. '★GAP 1★ a live holder's lock is NEVER stolen while it's still working past staleMs (heartbeat keeps it alive)' passed all 3 runs (~300ms each). 'PROP-101a: isLockStale never flags a heartbeat-refreshed lock as stale, however long total elapsed time grows' and 'PROP-101b: isLockStale boundary -- exactly staleMs elapsed is NOT stale, 1ms past IS stale' both present and passing, exercising isLockStale directly (not only through acquire()).

reclaimStaleLock() uses `await fs.rename(file, trashFile)` (a single atomic POSIX primitive) instead of the old unlink-then-open sequence; on ENOENT (lost the race) it returns false rather than proceeding. No check-then-act window: fs.rename's source-must-exist + atomicity-w.r.t.-concurrent-renames-of-the-same-source guarantee means exactly one racer's rename can succeed.

'★PROP-101c (Tier 2, atomicity)★ two concurrent stale-lock reclaim attempts on the SAME lock key -- exactly ONE must win, never both' re-run 3 consecutive times by the adversary (as part of the full 48/48 suite, 3 repetitions), passed every time with zero flakiness.

evidence.location: adversary-authored script (not from the builder's test files), /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/adversary-stress/stale-reclaim-stress.mjs
evidence.description: Independent 10-way stress test: created ONE genuinely stale lock file (backdated mtime), fired 10 concurrent withGigLock() callers at it. Re-run 3 times: winnersCount=1 every time (9 of 10 rejected with the fail-closed 'currently being processed' reason each run). This exceeds the builder's own 2-way atomicity test and confirms the atomic-reclaim guarantee holds under higher concurrency too.

Control-flow read of applyAndSave(): (a) `const state = await loadState(statePath);` happens INSIDE the withGigLock(BOARD_LOCK_KEY, ...) callback, i.e. freshly re-read from disk immediately before every mutation, never a stale in-memory snapshot; (b) the board lock's critical section is exactly {loadState, mutateFn, saveState} -- the network/settle step (pay()) happens BEFORE applyAndSave is even called, inside the per-gigId lock, never inside the board lock; (c) BOARD_LOCK_RETRY_ATTEMPTS/_DELAY_MS bounded retry is applied ONLY around applyAndSave's own withGigLock(BOARD_LOCK_KEY,...) call -- gigTake/gigDeliver/gigVerifyAndPay's own withGigLock(gigId,...) calls have no such retry wrapper, so a genuine same-gigId contention is still rejected outright on the first attempt (verified: no retry loop wraps any of the outer withGigLock(statePath, gigId, ...) call sites).
'★PROP-102a (3-way)★', '★PROP-102b★', '★PROP-102c★' all re-run 3 times by the adversary, all passing every run (durations ~140-270ms, no flakiness).

evidence.description: Independent 6-way cross-gigId stress test (beyond the builder's 3-way test): posted 6 distinct gigs A-F, took+delivered gig A, then fired 1 SLOW (150ms) verify_and_pay on gig A concurrently with 5 FAST takes on gigs B-F. Re-run 3 times: every run ended with gig A 'paid' and gigs B-F all 'taken' -- no clobbering, no lost update, despite the 5x wider concurrency than the builder's own test.

Independently re-run 3 consecutive times by the adversary: 48/48 pass every time (durations 990-1253ms), 0 fail, 0 flake. '★FINDING 1★ gig_verify_and_pay REJECTS a non-poster caller', '★FINDING 2★ two CONCURRENT gig_verify_and_pay(true) calls on the SAME gig pay out EXACTLY ONCE', '★FINDING 3★' (x3 identity tests) all present by name and passing.

summary: All 8 CRIT items PASS. lock.mjs's isLockStale extraction and atomic fs.rename-based reclaim are real and independently re-verified, including under adversary-authored concurrency beyond the builder's own tests (10-way stale-reclaim, 6-way cross-gigId). gig.mjs's applyAndSave genuinely re-reads fresh state under a board lock scoped only to the local read-mutate-write, with the bounded retry correctly scoped only to that shared lock (never per-gigId). The full pre-existing gig test suite is genuinely 48/48 green (re-run 3x by the adversary itself), and the round-1 fail-open exploits were independently re-attacked LIVE by this adversary against the real Base Sepolia facilitator + ERC-8004 registry, producing fresh, on-chain-verified transaction hashes distinct from and not reliant on the builder's prior round-3 self-report -- both attacks (self-verify, same-gig double-pay) were rejected exactly as designed. The catalog-gate is a genuinely pure, unscored, unranked bookkeeping filter; all 17 live registry.json slots are correctly tagged (independently re-derived against a sample of the underlying slots' own code, not merely trusted); the hl_trade fail-open and lazy-invocation behavior and the non-sticky restoration property are both real and test-covered. The business.blockrun.ai research record's claims were spot-checked against live, current state (gh PR, DNS, firecrawl) and all matched exactly. One non-blocking, informational finding (FIND-501) is recorded: the adversary's own live Tier-3 re-attack wrote into the SHARED gig-board witness state file (not a dedicated test path) after discovering gig-board/.env's GIG_STATE_PATH is shared production/witness infrastructure -- this has no bearing on the correctness of the code under review, but is flagged so the witness track's operators are aware the JSON snapshot no longer holds the original 2026-07-06 gigs (the facilitator's own append-only log still does). This sprint is APPROVED to proceed to Phase 5 (harden).
